thread.title: 3 Upbeat Stocks to Watch This Earnings Season

author: TipRanks
title: 3 Upbeat Stocks to Watch This Earnings Season
text:
Shutterstock photo We are now in the midst of earnings season- with around 125 S&P 500 companies reporting their results this week. Like most investors, we are keeping a close eye on the reports, to see who hits expectations and who falls short. The results will determine the shape of the market in the weeks – and possibly, months – to come.
According to CNBC, the earnings season so far is going well. The US-China trade tensions – which have eased in recent weeks – haven’t put much hurt on anyone, with the notable exception of Apple ( AAPL ). Going by the numbers, we’re seeing some three-fourths of companies report earnings that beat the expectations. That’s versus 24.1% of companies missing analysts' expectations according to data from Refinitiv. It’s a solid showing, and it’s giving a bump to a market that was already showing gains.
Now let’s dip into the TipRanks database , and see what Wall Street’s analysts think of the earnings prospects for some top stocks.
Google This
With a market cap of over $760 billion, Google parent company Alphabet, Inc. ( GOOGL – Research Report ) is the third largest publicly traded entity in the world. In a recent survey of online search engine and social media use, Google’s audience reported the most stability, with 96% of those surveyed saying they use the Google site, and 95% saying that their use of Google as remained steady or increased in the past six months.
With near-total market penetration, and a stable user base, Google and its subsidiaries have a firm foundation to build advertising revenues. So, it may be a surprise that GOOGL stock has ended 2018 almost exactly where it began: trading at $1,100 per share. Despite the share price having dipped recently, GOOGL is looking at a strong fourth quarter report.
The strength of that quarter will be obvious on February 4, when Alphabet releases its Q4 FY2018 earnings. The company is expected to post EPS at $11.12, for 6.9% year-over-year growth. The quarterly revenues, at $31.26 billion, are expected to show a 20.8% increase from the year-ago quarter.
The upbeat expectations are behind five-star Stifel analyst Scott Devitt’s ( Track Record & Ratings ) $1,300 price target on GOOGL stock. That’s an 18% upside potential, which is doubly impressive given the already high value of the shares. Regarding the upcoming earnings, Devitt says, “…he expects Alphabet to grow total net revenue 20.5% in Q4, which is roughly in line with the consensus forecast.”
Heading into earnings season, GOOGL has a ‘Strong Buy’ analyst consensus, based on a unanimous 18 ‘buy’ ratings. The average price target is $1,352, giving a 22% upside to the current share price of $1,101.
Amdocs, Beating the Rumors
Switching gears from Google to Amdocs, Ltd. ( DOX – Research Report ), a mid-cap tech company that provides software and services for the communications, entertainment, and pay TV industries. Amdocs investors had a bit of fright recently, when the stock tumbled 9% on January 24.
The sharp loss reflected worries that Amdocs is resorting to, er, “fancy” accounting techniques to show healthy growth in the lead-up to the Q1 FY2019 earnings release – however, those rumors came from short position holders in the company, who have an incentive, or at least a desire, to see the stock price decline.
Don’t necessarily expect that decline, however. DOX shares stabilized quickly in the last two trading sessions, and the earnings forecasts – the report is due out on February 5 – are moderately robust. While the 90 cent expected EPS is lower that last year’s 97 cents, total estimated revenues, at $1.01 billion, are significantly higher than last year’s $977.7 million.
Amdocs has a good reputation in its industry, a fact pointed out by Shaul Eyal ( Track Record & Ratings ), of Oppenheimer. Writing of the stock recently, Eyal said, “We believe the company is experiencing healthy demand trends, and remains an innovation leader, supporting its customers on their path to digital transformation.”
Eyal elaborated on Amdocs’ optimistic outlook: “New capabilities enabled by technological advances along with consumers’ demands for more choices, faster service, and an enhanced customer experience should prompt service providers to seek out the best partners, such as DOX.” His price target for the stock is $77, suggesting a 39% upside potential.
Overall, DOX gets a ‘Moderate Buy’ consensus rating, based on 2 ‘buy’ and 1 ‘hold’ rating. The stock has a 36% upside, with an average price target of $75 and a current share price of $55.
Time to Make the Donuts
Of course, on your way to work at the high-techs, you gotta stop for breakfast. Which means, Dunkin’ Brands Group, Inc. ( DNKN – Research Report ). Dunkin’ Donuts, before the chain rebranded itself as simply Dunkin’. The products remain the same, however: a range of tasty donuts, good breakfast sandwiches on bread or bagels, Baskin-Robbins ice cream, and most importantly, the same great coffee at the same low price. It’s a model that has served this company well for decades, and developed a loyal following.
That loyal following of donut-and-coffee lovers has powered a 45% increase in sales for Q4 FY2018 compared to Q4 last year. Estimates for quarterly sales range from $322 million to $345 million; last year’s reported Q4 number was $227.14 million. For the full fiscal year, Dunkin’ Brands is expected to report $1.33 billion in total revenue. The full report is to be released on February 7.
Quite a good showing, for a coffee shop.
DNKN’s solid hold on its niche has generated plenty of positive notice from the market analysts, with buy ratings and high price targets set every month since October. The most recent buy, from five-star analyst Stephen Anderson ( Track Record & Ratings ) of Maxim Group, sets an $83 price target, giving the stock a 19% upside potential. Anderson described the stock as “our defensive pick,” a strong hedge against declining overall market performance.
Even DNKN’s weakest recent review, a ‘hold’ rating given on January 23 by Cowen Analyst Andrew Charles ( Track Record & Ratings ) gives the stock a 5% upside and an increase to the price target, from $71 to $73. Charles says, referring to the recent rebranding, “Checks suggest optimism around brand direction.”
DNKN’s average price target, $80, suggests a 16% upside to the share price of $69. The stock holds a ‘Strong Buy’ from the analyst consensus, with 3 ‘buy’ ratings and only that 1 ‘hold.’
And now I’m going to go get a donut.
Author: Michael Marcus
